chapters.title: A. What is science?
key_concepts: A. What is science?
Why does the apple fall to the ground?
Scientists always want to know why and how it happens.
The study of phenomena and events in Nature through systematic observation and experimentation is called science.
Science enables us to answer many questions in Nature.
How are northern lights formed?
Where do I come from?
Why does iron rust?
B. The branches of science
Physics the study of matter, energy and forces
Chemistry the study of the properties, composition, structure and reactions of matter
Biology the study of living things
Astronomy the study of the Sun, the Moon, the stars and the Universe
Geology the study of the structure of the Earth
Medicine the study of the human body and diseases
___________ is the study of phenomena and events in Nature through systematic observation and experimentation.
There are different branches of science.
C. Application and impact of science
1. Scientific discoveries and inventions
In the 19th century, Louis Pasteur discovered that …
microoganisms can cause diseases
scientific discovery
Louis Pasteur’s discoveries led to the invention of …
vaccines of some diseases
scientific invention

Another great invention of Louis Pasteur is pasteurization. It is a technique of heating wine or milk to a particular temperature and then quickly cooling it. This can keep the drink fresh for a longer time.
Other inventions have greatly improved the quality of our lives. Can you give some examples?

chapters.title: A. Steps in scientific investigations
key_concepts: A. Steps in scientific investigations
How do scientists work to find things out?
Let’s read the story of the famous scientist Galileo to see how scientists work.
In the past, people believed that heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects.
Galileo observed that hailstones of different sizes fell to the ground at the same time.
hailstones of different sizes
He then formed a hypothesis to explain what he observed.
Perhaps all objects have the same falling speed.
An experiment was done to test his hypothesis. Two balls of different masses were dropped from the top of a tower.
It was found that the two balls fell to the ground at the same time.
He analysed the results and drew a conclusion.
Heavy and light objects fall at the same speed.
Scientists find things out by conducting scientific investigations.
They first observe carefully and systematically.
Then, they form a hypothesis (plural: hypotheses) to explain the observations.
Form a hypothesis
They test the hypothesis by doing experiments.
Design and do experiments
Finally, they analyse the experimental results and draw a conclusion.
Draw a conclusion
Science is based on evidence.
Scientists try to find evidence (including observations and data) in the experiments to support their hypothesis.
enough evidence  hypothesis is correct and becomes acceptable scientific knowledge
Results support the hypothesis
Becomes acceptable scientific knowledge
if new evidence is found  scientific knowledge can be disproved
Results not support the hypothesis
Modify the hypothesis
Steps in a scientific investigation
When we study science, we should not regard scientific knowledge only as facts to memorize.

Science is the study of phenomena and events in Nature through systematic observation and experimentation.
1.1 Learning about science

key_concepts: A. Change in the physical states of water
Water can exist in three physical states.

The change from solid state to liquid state is called melting.
Melting takes place at a fixed temperature. This temperature is called the melting point. The melting point of ice is 0 °C.
When ice melts, it absorbs energy.
The change from liquid state to solid state is called freezing.
Freezing takes place at a fixed temperature. This temperature is called the freezing point. The freezing point of water is 0 °C.
When water freezes, it releases energy.
The change from liquid state to gas state is called boiling.
Boiling takes place at a fixed temperature. This temperature is called the boiling point. The boiling point of water is 100 °C.
When water boils, it absorbs energy.
Water can change its state from liquid to gas lower than the boiling point. This process is called evaporation.
Wet clothes become dry as water evaporates.
When we get out of the water, we feel cold because water on our skin evaporates and absorbs energy from our bodies.
When water evaporates, it absorbs energy.
Water can change its state from gas to liquid through condensation.
When water vapour or steam condenses into water, it releases energy.
When the water vapour in air comes into contact with cold surfaces, it condenses into water, forming water droplets on the surfaces.

How long can people survive without water?

They flipped the boat over but the engine of the boat was damaged. They lost their food and drinking water.
The engine is damaged!

key_concepts: In Hong Kong, the fresh water we use comes from Dongjiang water and rainwater.
How is the water treated before it is supplied to the public?
The diagram below summarizes the key steps in water treatment in Hong Kong.
water (Dongjiang water and rainwater)
Water (Dongjiang water and rainwater) is first filtered through screens to remove large objects (e.g. fish, leaves and rubbish).
Alum is added to the water and mixed in a rapid mixing chamber. This makes the insoluble impurities in water stick together.
rapid mixing chamber
The water then passes into a sedimentation tank, where insoluble impurities sink. The sediment is collected and removed.
sedimentation tank
After sedimentation, the water is filtered through layers of sands and gravel in a filtration tank. Small and suspended insoluble impurities that remain are thus removed.

filtration tank

A. Vital functions of living things
The seven vital functions below are common to all living things.
Living things need food for energy and nutrients.
A giant panda needs to eat 12 to 38 kg of bamboo a day.
Plants can make their own food by photosynthesis.
Living things need to breathe. They use the oxygen in the air to break down food to provide energy, in a process called respiration.
A seal can hold its breath underwater for almost an hour. Then, it goes up to the surface to breathe.
Mangrove plants can take in oxygen through aerial roots.
Living things can move.
The cheetah is the fastest runner on land. It can run 100 m in less than 6 seconds.
bud of sunflower
The bud of a sunflower turns towards the Sun slowly during the day.
Living things can grow.
A baby kangaroo is less than 2.5 cm long when it is born. It can grow to 2.6 m tall as an adult.
Bamboo is one of the fastest growing plants in the world. It can grow as much as 90 cm each day.
Living things can detect and react to stimuli in the environment.
An eagle can see a fish 3 km away and swoop down to catch it.
The shy plant responds to touch by folding its leaves.
Living things remove waste from their bodies.

A. History of the use of metals
According to the main types of materials used by humans, historians divided human history into four main different periods, namely The Stone Age, The Copper Age, The Bronze Age and The Iron Age.
Stones could be commonly found in Nature and easily obtained by humans. Humans then used stones to make tools and weapons and The Stone Age came first in human history.

The discovery and use of metals are related to their ease of extraction and abundance.
Copper is much easier to be extracted than tin and iron. As a result, The Copper Age came earlier than The Bronze Age and The Iron Age in human history.

（公元前250萬年至公元前4000年）
石頭在大自然中十分常見，很容易便取得。因此人類最先使用石頭來製造各種工具和武器，石器時代因而在人類歷史中最先開始。
（公元前4000年至公元前3000年）
人類懂得從礦石中提取銅，並開始使用銅來製造工具和武器等。銅比石頭容易製造出不同形狀的工具和武器。
（公元前3000年至公元前1000年）

人類開始懂得怎樣從鐵礦中提取鐵。鐵在地球上的藴藏量很高，而且較青銅堅硬，因此鐵逐漸取代了青銅，成為最常用的材料。

三稜鏡可用來反射光線，當中涉及 全內反射。三稜鏡可用於貓眼石、 安全反光板、稜鏡潛望鏡和雙筒望 遠鏡中。
與全內反射有關的例子包括鑽石閃 閃發亮、光沿光纖傳播，以及水中 的視野。
當平行於主軸的光線通過凸透鏡後，光線會 會聚於主焦點；當平行於主軸的光線通過凹 透鏡後，光線會看似從主焦點發散。
凸透鏡的成像具有不同的性質。凹透鏡成像 的性質是正立、縮小和虛像。
實像可用屏幕捕捉，虛像則不可。
放大率可用來比較物體與成像的大小。
凸透鏡可用於放大鏡、顯微鏡、相機 和矯正遠視的眼鏡，凹透鏡則可用於 防盜眼和矯正近視的眼鏡。
「光」代表一種波，稱為電磁波。
不同種類的電磁波有不同的波長。
白光通過三稜鏡時會發生色散，形成 色譜（亦稱為可見光譜）。
把原色光按不同的比例混合，可產生 任何色光。
物體呈現的顏色取決於它反射的色光。
紅外輻射存在於可見光譜上紅光以外 的位置，紫外輻射則存在於可見光譜 上紫光以外的位置。
